title: Fast CZ gate in hybrid fluxonium-transmon systems with tunable couplers
authors: Peng Xu, Yunlong Wang, Yuechen Mu, Ling Jiang, Peng Zhao, Shengjun Wu, Xiaohong Yan
abstract: Hybrid superconducting architectures combining different types of qubits offer a promising platform for exploiting their complementary advantages, yet high-fidelity entangling gates remain challenging because of strong nonlinearities and residual qubit-qubit interactions. Here, we propose a high-fidelity controlled-Z (CZ) gate for a hybrid circuit comprising a fluxonium qubit, a fixed-frequency transmon qubit, and a flux-tunable transmon coupler. By modulating only the external magnetic flux applied to the coupler, the qubit-qubit interaction is dynamically engineered for conditional-phase accumulation while the residual interaction is suppressed at idle, mitigating spectator-induced errors. We employ a low-dimensional Fourier-cosine pulse parameterization and a physically motivated cost function to independently suppress conditional-phase errors and leakage from the computational subspace. Numerical simulations demonstrate that a microwave-free CZ gate can be realized within $25 \mathrm{ns}$, with an average gate fidelity exceeding $99.99\%$ and leakage below $10^{-5}$. Using experimentally relevant superconducting-qubit parameters and accounting for decoherence, the proposed scheme maintains a CZ-gate fidelity of approximately $99.9\%$. We further extend the analysis to larger coupled architectures and find that the CZ-gate infidelity remains below $10^{-4}$ in the presence of spectator qubits. These results establish single-parameter flux control as a simple and robust approach for realizing high-fidelity entangling gates in heterogeneous superconducting quantum architectures.
summary: This paper proposes a robust, single-parameter flux control scheme to implement a high-fidelity Controlled-Z gate in hybrid superconducting circuits combining fluxonium and transmon qubits. By dynamically tuning the coupler via external magnetic flux, the authors suppress unwanted residual interactions while accumulating the necessary conditional phase. The results show fast gate operation (25 ns) with fidelity exceeding 99.9%, validating this approach for complex quantum hardware.
main_problem: The primary challenge is realizing a high-fidelity Controlled-Z (CZ) gate in complex, hybrid superconducting quantum architectures.
main_result: The authors demonstrate a microwave-free CZ gate achievable in 25 ns with fidelities exceeding 99.99% in simulations, establishing single-parameter flux control as a robust method.
method: The method involves dynamically engineering the qubit-qubit interaction by modulating the external magnetic flux applied to a tunable coupler, optimizing the pulse shape using Fourier-cosine parameterization.
model_or_system: The system is a hybrid circuit composed of a fluxonium qubit, a fixed-frequency transmon qubit, and a flux-tunable transmon coupler. The Hamiltonian is controlled by the external magnetic flux applied to the coupler.
key_observables: Average gate fidelity (target > 99.9%), leakage error (target < 10^-5), and the conditional phase accumulation ($\phi_{cond}$).
important_parameters: Gate time ($\approx 25 	ext{ ns}$), coupling strengths ($J_{TF}, J_{TC}, J_{FC}$), and the external magnetic flux $\Phi_{	ext{ext}}(t)$.
main_assumptions: The approach relies on single-parameter flux control for simplicity and robustness, and the analysis accounts for decoherence effects.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the schematic of the coupled TCF circuit, while Figure 2(b) shows how varying the external flux causes avoided crossings, which are key to understanding the interaction and leakage.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical challenge in hybrid systems, details the Hamiltonian and the flux-tuning methodology, presents the optimization procedure to suppress errors, and concludes with high-fidelity performance metrics.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, hardware-agnostic protocol for high-fidelity quantum gates in heterogeneous superconducting platforms, which is highly relevant for quantum information scientists designing next-generation quantum processors.
